sources: Official list: Exophase (exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/) and PSNProfiles (psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi), frozen 2026-11-18, agreeing on every name, description and grade. Hidden flags cross-checked against planetgta6.com and outputlag.com, both drawn from the same official list. Guides are our own words from the official descriptions; a method that names another guide cites it, and anything not yet checked in the game says so.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the reward for everything else on this list: there is no shortcut, no separate task and no way to buy it. Earn the other 54 trophies and this one pops on its own. Plan the run around the two long grinds, 250 stunts and 100% completion, and around the one trophy you can genuinely miss, Positive Mental Attitude, whose Chapter 1 meditation disappears when the chapter ends. Keep a manual save at the start of every chapter and one from just before the final mission, because the game has no mission replay. Community estimates put the platinum at around 200 hours; it is long rather than hard, with no online, difficulty or mission-medal trophies anywhere on the list. Use the roadmap and the Next up planner here to work through the list in order instead of wandering.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Time estimate: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: This is the opening mission, Gone Fishing, and the trophy is unmissable: finish the mission and it pops. It is the first story trophy most players will earn, and it sets up the rest of Chapter 1. There is nothing to prepare and nothing to miss; just play the story. If you are tracking progress, tick it off as soon as the mission ends and move on to Paradise Lost, which is the Chapter 1 completion trophy. The mission also introduces fishing, which matters later for Baited My Tackle, so pay attention to how the fishing challenge works while you are here.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1 and the trophy pops. Chapter trophies can pop at the start of the next chapter rather than on the last cutscene, so do not worry if it arrives a beat late. Chapter 1 is also where the one genuinely missable moment in the game lives: Lucia's balcony meditation, which counts toward Positive Mental Attitude and is gone once the chapter ends. Before you finish Chapter 1, do that meditation (it happens in the morning after the mission Down to Earth, when Lucia heads to the balcony of Jason's house) and keep a manual save from the start of the chapter until the trophy pops. Everything else in Chapter 1 can be revisited or finished later.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Missable detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies it is unmissable and can pop as the next chapter begins. Chapter 2 is where the game opens up: switching between Jason and Lucia becomes available right after the mission Breakfast Run, and most of the list only becomes reachable once both characters are playable, so several trophies need the two of them together. Two things unlock here that matter for the rest of the run: the Vice City Real Estate app, after the mission Daily Driver, which sells the eight garages for Little Boxes, and the Scooter Bros app, after the mission Moses, which you need for On the Spot. Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter, as with every chapter, because there is no mission replay.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Unlock details: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. Unmissable, and it can pop as Chapter 4 begins. Two things in this chapter deserve a save before you do them. First, the mission Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs gives you the Snap Gun and opens jewelry store robberies, which you need for Sneakthief. Second, the street race against Yago in Yago's racing strand is time-sensitive, marked with an hourglass icon, and the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks, so save first and race the moment it appears. Robbery tools start arriving in the middle of the game, so the robbery trophies begin to open up from here, but the bank vaults themselves do not unlock until near the end of Chapter 4.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Method details: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4. Unmissable, and it can pop as the final chapter begins. Near the end of this chapter the optional mission That's Where The Money Is unlocks the bank vaults, which you need for Maximum Withdrawal, and the vault escapes also feed Hot Together and A Classic Blitz Play. Before you push into the final mission, make a manual save you never overwrite: there is no mission replay and no new game plus, so a save from just before the finale is your only way back to anything you missed in the story. Once the story is done, everything outside it stays available, including the side-story finales and the 100% completion checklist, which only appears under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion after the credits.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Method details: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission and this gold trophy pops. It is unmissable once you reach the finale, and it is one of only two golds on the list, the other being A Long Road for 100% completion. The important preparation happens before you start the finale: keep an untouched manual save from just before it. The game has no mission replay, so without that save you cannot replay the ending, and several trophies are easier to mop up from a pre-finale save than from a fresh playthrough. After the credits, the whole map stays open, the side-story finales stay available, and the 100% checklist appears, so the finale is a doorway into the cleanup phase, not the end of the run.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Save advice: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run. It is unmissable, and it matters beyond its own trophy: switching between Jason and Lucia opens right after this mission, and from then on you can switch characters and call the other in as your partner. Several trophies need the pair together, Hot Together, Retail Therapy and Personal Best among them, so Breakfast Run is effectively the moment the full trophy list opens up. Just play the story until the mission ends; there is nothing to prepare, and nothing about this trophy can be missed.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Switching detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist. Unmissable: play the story and it pops when the mission ends. Heist missions tend to be the longest and most involved in a chapter, so expect a multi-stage job rather than a quick errand, and keep a manual save from the start of the chapter in case anything goes wrong. The Cartel Heist is one of the six named story-mission trophies on the list, alongside Breakfast Run, Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown and Operation Savage Glory, and all six work the same way: complete the mission, collect the trophy, move on.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play. Unmissable, and it pops when the mission ends. There is no preparation and no way to miss it; the only advice that applies is the general story advice for this whole list: keep a manual save at the start of every chapter, because the game has no mission replay and no new game plus. If a mission ever feels like it went wrong, reloading that chapter-start save is cheaper than replaying the game. Child's Play is one of the six named story-mission trophies, and like the others it is simply a marker that you played through that part of the story.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners. Unmissable: complete the mission and the trophy pops. The name is written exactly as PlayStation publishes it, in capitals, and the trophy is hidden on PlayStation until you earn it, which is why this guide keeps story trophies behind the spoiler setting until they are earned. Headliners sits in the middle of the story, so by the time you reach it you will already have character switching, the partner system and most of the map open. Nothing about this mission feeds any other trophy, so there is no special preparation beyond the usual chapter-start save.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown. Unmissable, and it pops when the mission ends. The mission takes place around Vice City International Airport, the same airport where the free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can lives, so after the mission it is worth remembering the layout: the large passenger planes docked at the boarding bridges, at gates E3 and E4, are the ones that count for the unscheduled departure. But the mission itself needs no preparation. Keep your chapter-start save, finish the mission, and the trophy is yours.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Airport detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Unmissable, and it pops when the mission ends. It is the last of the six named story-mission trophies, and it lands late in the story, so by now the robbery tools, the partner system and the full map are all available. After this mission you are close to the finale, which is the right moment to check the missable watch list in this guide: Positive Mental Attitude is the only trophy with a confirmed missable moment, and its Chapter 1 meditation is long past by now, so if you did not do it, your chapter-start save from Chapter 1 is the way back. Otherwise, finish the mission and keep pushing toward the final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion. This is the second gold on the list and the longest grind in the game. The 100% checklist only appears after the story, under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion, but work you do earlier still counts, so start early and let it accumulate. The checklist covers the story, the collectibles and the activities, and its targets are stricter than the individual trophies: 300 stunts instead of 250, 200 of the 277 vehicle models instead of 100, 70 of the 80 challenges instead of 50, all eight bank vaults instead of five, and all 39 illegal operations instead of one per gang. The practical approach is to finish the story first, then work the roadmap stages in this guide in order, using the counters here to track each target. It will not pop until the very last item on the checklist is done.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · 100% targets: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunt jumps, under-the-bridge flights, knife flights and base jumps all count, so the fastest way to build the total is to attempt a stunt whenever you travel instead of driving straight to the objective. Use the counter in this guide to track progress. The trophy pops at 250, but keep going: 100% completion needs 300 stunts, so stopping at 250 leaves work for later. Stunts are pure practice, and the risk is only wasted time, so attempt them in free roam between missions rather than in the middle of a story job. A stunt plane or a fast bike makes the aerial stunts much easier than a car.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 250) · Stunt types and 100% target: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. The game tracks nine activity types, and the trophy pops when you have tried the ninth. The activities are the things the world offers outside the story: races, fishing, arcade games, drone races, the shooting range, bowling, meditation, hunting and the rest of the side content. The practical approach is variety: every time you try something new, check whether the counter moved, and do not repeat one activity expecting progress. Most players will earn this naturally while working through the other activity trophies, since the list is built so that trying everything once is the first step toward mastering each of them. If it has not popped, the counter in this guide shows how many types you have tried.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 9) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. The medals are spread across two shooting ranges, 42 golds between them. Each challenge grades speed and accuracy, so the two skills to practice are fast target acquisition and controlled bursts rather than spraying. Use the weapon the challenge gives you, learn the target pattern on a first run, then push for gold on the second. This is one of the few trophies on the list that is genuinely skill-gated rather than time-gated, so expect to repeat the harder challenges. Work through the ranges in order and use the counter here to see which medals are still missing. There is no way to miss this trophy; the ranges stay open after the story.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 42) · Range detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location. There are 14 drone race locations, and you need a win at each one, not just 14 wins anywhere. Drone racing is its own skill: learn the course on a first attempt, then race it cleanly. The drones handle differently from every other vehicle in the game, so expect the first few races to feel awkward and the later ones to click once the controls make sense. Keep a note of which locations you have already won, or use the counter here, because the trophy only cares about coverage: one win per location, all 14. The races stay available after the story, so there is no rush and nothing to miss.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 14) · Location count: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Each distinct race counts once, so winning the same race twenty times does nothing; you need twenty different events. Street races, circuit races and the other race types around Leonida all count, and the time-sensitive race against Yago in Chapter 3 is one of them, so do that one the moment it appears and keep a save first. The practical approach is to work through the race locations as you explore, one new race at a time, and let the counter here show which ones are done. Races stay available after the story, so the only race with any urgency is Yago's, and even that only matters because its strand feeds Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 20) · Yago detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is introduced in the opening mission Gone Fishing, so you will already know the basics by the time Cal challenges you: cast, wait for the bite, and work the line without snapping it. The challenge against Cal is a head-to-head contest rather than a free fishing session, so the skill that matters is landing the fish cleanly and quickly. If you lose, try again; fishing challenges can be repeated, and there is nothing missable here. Do it whenever the challenge appears, and remember that fishing itself is one of the nine activity types for Master of None, so this trophy also feeds that counter.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete an arcade game. Any of the four in-game arcade games counts, so pick the one you enjoy most and play it through to the end. Arcade games are found in the arcades around Leonida, and completing one means finishing a full game rather than just starting it. This is one of the quickest trophies on the list and one of the nine activity types for Master of None, so it is worth doing early, when you are still sampling everything the world offers. There is no difficulty requirement and nothing to miss; the arcades stay open after the story.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Arcade detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy. Andy is one of the side characters with a mission strand of his own, and this trophy pops when you finish the last mission in that strand. Side-story finales stay open after the story ends, so there is no deadline and nothing to miss; you can do Andy's strand whenever it appears and finish it at your own pace. One thing to know: Andy's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks, because it has its own trophy. That is true of the Billy and Tyrone strands too. Check the trophy counter after each strand you finish to see what counted, and work through the side characters one at a time.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Strand detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton. Kenton's strand is one of the side stories that stays open after the main story ends, so finish it whenever you are ready; there is no deadline and nothing missable. The title is a hint at the tone of the finale, and the mission itself is the last in a chain, so if Kenton's missions have not appeared yet, keep playing the story and exploring: side strands unlock as the chapters progress. Like the other side finales, this one is a self-contained chain, and completing it is simply a matter of following the strand to its end.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy. Billy's strand is another side story that stays open after the main story, so there is no rush and nothing to miss. Billy's missions do not count toward Strangers & Freaks, because the strand has its own trophy, just like Andy's and Tyrone's. Work through the strand when it appears, finish the finale, and the trophy pops. If you are chasing the platinum efficiently, do the side strands as they unlock rather than leaving them all for the post-story cleanup, because they are spread across the map and pair naturally with the collectibles and activities nearby.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Strand detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Not every stranger questline counts: the strands for Andy, Billy and Tyrone have their own trophies and do not feed this counter, so you need eight other strands. Check the trophy's progress counter after each strand you finish to see what counted. The time-sensitive race against Yago in Chapter 3 belongs to a strand that does count, and it is marked with an hourglass icon, so save first and race it the moment it appears. Stranger strands appear as you explore and progress the story, so the practical approach is to take every stranger mission you meet, finish the strand, and watch the counter. There is no deadline on the strands themselves; they stay open after the story.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 8) · Strand and Yago details: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy. Randy's strand is one of the side stories that stays open after the main story ends, so finish it at your own pace; there is nothing missable and no deadline. Side strands unlock as the story progresses, so if Randy's missions have not appeared yet, keep playing and exploring and check back. The finale is the last mission in the chain, and the trophy pops when it ends. Like the other side finales, this one pairs well with the collectibles and activities in the same part of the map, so do it while you are already out there rather than making a separate trip.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone. Tyrone's strand is a side story that stays open after the main story, so there is no deadline and nothing to miss. Like Andy's and Billy's strands, Tyrone's does not count toward Strangers & Freaks, because it has its own trophy. Finish the chain, and the trophy pops at the finale. If you are working through the side characters in order, Tyrone's strand is one of five named finales on the list, alongside Andy, Kenton, Billy and Randy, and all five work the same way: follow the strand, finish the last mission, collect the trophy.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Strand detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida. There are 18 meditation spots, and this is the one trophy on the list with a confirmed missable moment, so read this carefully. In Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, Lucia heads out to the balcony of Jason's house in the morning to meditate; follow her and accept the optional task. That balcony meditation is gone once Chapter 1 ends. It is not confirmed that the trophy strictly needs it, but do it anyway and keep a Chapter 1 manual save until the trophy pops. The other spots show as purple icons when you are close, and each outdoor spot should count twice if you meditate there with both characters, so bring your partner every time. Do the Chapter 1 spot first, then work the rest with the counter here.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 18) · Missable detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret Vogel's hunting questline is Jason-only, and it sends you after animals through target decks, one target at a time. A clean head or heart shot keeps the carcass pristine, which matters for the hunt, so take your time, aim carefully and do not rush the shot. Hunting is one of the nine activity types for Master of None, so this strand feeds that counter too. The questline stays available after the story, so there is no deadline and nothing to miss. Work through the target decks in order, and the trophy pops when the unique animal is hunted for Bret.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Hunting detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three collectible card sets. The cards are scattered around Leonida, and a set is complete when you hold every card in it. This is a pure collectible grind: explore, pick up cards as you find them, and use the counter here to track how many sets are done. There is no trick to it and nothing missable; the cards stay where they are after the story, so you can finish this in the cleanup phase. The practical approach is to grab cards whenever you are already in an area for another reason, a mission, a race or a robbery, rather than hunting them all in one dedicated sweep. Three full sets is the target, and the trophy pops on the third.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 3) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game app you use to tag places, and the trophy is a coverage grind: open the app at a hundred different spots around Leonida and tag each one. The habit that makes this painless is to tag a location every time you arrive somewhere new, instead of saving it all for the end. WAiNK also scans vehicles, and scanning a vehicle counts as discovering it for Whip It Good, so the two trophies feed each other: tag locations as you travel, scan the traffic as you drive, and both counters climb together. Nothing here is missable, and the locations stay available after the story.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 100) · WAiNK detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are listed under Progress, then Challenges, and they cover almost everything you do in the game, from driving and shooting to exploring and robbing. Many of them complete on their own while you play, so the counter climbs without any special effort through the first half of the run. The trophy pops at 50, but keep going: 100% completion needs 70 of the 80 challenges, so stopping at 50 leaves work for later. Once the easy ones are done, open the challenge list, pick the nearest unfinished ones, and clear them deliberately. Nothing here is missable; challenges stay available after the story.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 50) · Challenge detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a four-star wanted level with your partner and escape the heat. The easiest way to get four stars with your partner beside you is a bank vault job: escaping a vault gives you four stars straight away, so the vault run and this trophy pair naturally. The trophy pops once you have left the red heat zone, not just the flashing search area, so keep driving until you are fully clear. Make sure your partner is actually with you when the heat starts; call them in before the job. If the stars drop before you escape, the attempt fails and you will need another four-star chase. It is repeatable, so a failed escape costs nothing but time.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Vault and heat detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. Call your partner in, then rob three shops in a row while the police are still chasing you. The chain breaks if the stars fade and you are only in the red heat zone, so keep the heat alive between shops and do not linger. Pick three shops close together so the run between them is short, and have your getaway planned before you start. The trophy can take about thirty seconds to pop after you leave the third shop, so give it a moment before you hit a fourth. If the chain breaks, set it up again; it is repeatable and nothing is missable.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 3) · Method: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Scanning a vehicle with the WAiNK app counts as discovering it, so the habit is simple: scan traffic as you drive. Every new model you scan adds to the counter, and the trophy pops at 100. Keep scanning past that, because 100% completion needs 200 of the 277 base models. This pairs perfectly with You WAiNKer!, which wants you to tag 100 locations: tag places as you arrive, scan vehicles as you pass them, and both counters climb on the same journeys. Nothing is missable and the traffic never runs out, so this is one of the most relaxed trophies on the list.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 100) · Scanning detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aim: press L3 and R3 while aiming. The trick is to find a group of enemies before you trigger it, such as the guards at an illegal operation, then activate Focus and take them down with an assault rifle while time is slowed. Adrenaline extends Focus, so keep the pressure on and do not waste the window. If you only get three or four, set it up again; the trophy is repeatable and illegal operations give you plenty of grouped enemies to practice on. Pick a spot with cover, trigger Focus with the group in view, and count your shots.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 5) · Combat Focus detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport. Steal a large passenger plane that is docked at a boarding bridge; planes parked elsewhere on the airfield do not count. The planes at gates E3 and E4 work. Go up to the cockpit, back out toward the runway and take off. The trophy is delayed: fly about one kilometre away from the airport and it pops. Save first, because the police come fast once you are in the plane. This is a free-roam trophy with no mission attached, so you can attempt it whenever you are near the airport, and you can retry it as often as you like if the first attempt goes wrong.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Method: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Get into a military tank, a Rhino. Tanks should be parked on the south side of Mile Zero Air Station, on the island at the far southwest of the map. Save first, get in, and drive and fire until the trophy pops. The description is a joke about the heat inside the tank, and the trophy is as simple as it sounds: find one, climb in, use it. The air station is a military area, so expect attention once you are inside, but the tank itself is the answer to that attention. This is a free-roam trophy with no mission attached and nothing missable; if you cannot find a tank on your first visit, come back and try again.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Location: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. The Chapter 3 mission Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs gives you the Snap Gun and opens jewelry store robberies, so you cannot do this before that mission. Go to a store's locked back door and use the Snap Gun on it; kicking the door in sets off the alarm, so do not force it. Inside the back room, find the note with the safe code, open the safe, and leave without being seen. Richardson Jewelry and Diamonds in Vice City is a good target. If someone spots you, reload rather than push on, because detection fails the attempt. It is repeatable, so a failed run costs nothing but the setup.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Method: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape. Bank vaults unlock through That's Where The Money Is, an optional mission near the end of Chapter 4, so you cannot start this before then. Tail an armored security van to a large bank and get into the vault while the guard has it open. You cannot carry all the bags alone, so bring your partner. Vault jobs give you a four-star wanted level straight away, so escaping one with your partner also earns Hot Together. The trophy pops at five vaults, but 100% completion needs all eight, so keep robbing after this pops. Each vault escape is also a chance to practice the getaway: leave the red heat zone fully, not just the flashing search area.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 5) · Vault detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks travel the roads of Leonida, and the job is to stop one, take what it carries, and get away. The same tailing skill you use for the bank vaults applies here: follow the truck, pick your moment, and hit it where you have room to escape. Like the other robbery trophies, this one only pops once you have left the red heat zone, not just the flashing search area, so keep driving until you are fully clear before you relax. It is repeatable, so a failed attempt costs nothing but time. Do it alongside the vault robberies, since the trucks and the vaults share the same getaway habits.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Heat-zone detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida. There are 52 areas to visit, and the trophy pops when you have been to all of them. The practical approach is to explore as you play rather than saving it for the end: every mission, race, robbery and collectible hunt takes you somewhere new, and the map fills in as you go. Use the in-game map to spot the gaps, then drive or fly through the areas you have not visited. A plane or helicopter makes the far corners much faster than a car. Nothing here is missable and nothing is locked behind the story, so the last few areas can be mopped up in the post-story cleanup along with the remaining collectibles.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 52) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang. There are nine gangs, and you need one operation from each, not nine operations from one gang. Illegal operations are the gang-run spots around Leonida, and each one belongs to a specific gang, so the work is coverage: hit one operation per gang and watch the counter. The trophy pops at nine, but 100% completion wants all 39 operations, so keep robbing after this pops. Operations also feed the other robbery trophies: their guards make good targets for Gunslinger, and the marked bills from the bigger jobs feed Dime on the Dollar. Work through the gangs as you explore, one operation at a time.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 9) · Gang and operation detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is one of the quiet world trophies: no mission, no chase, just a moment in a specific place. Head to Ocean Beach, find a spot with a view of the water, and have a cocktail there. It is the kind of trophy that rewards slowing down and looking around, and it is easy to miss if you only ever drive through Ocean Beach on the way to somewhere else. There is nothing to prepare and nothing missable; the beach and its bars stay open after the story, so stop by whenever you are nearby and take the moment. The ellipsis in the name is part of the official title as PlayStation publishes it.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Drive a vehicle through the front of a showroom and out onto the street, in the spirit of the classic scene this trophy is named for. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or drive one straight through the glass, and keep going until you are out. The trophy is about the spectacle rather than the damage, so commit to it: a half-hearted nudge will not do. There is no mission attached and nothing missable; showrooms stay open after the story, so you can attempt this whenever you are passing one. Expect the police to take an interest, so plan your exit route before you smash in.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. The alley is Kingpin Bowling, an illegal operation you visit in Chapter 2. Bring Sticky Bombs. Take all three key valuables: the luxury watch in an office, the shotgun on a table, and the contents of the office safe, which you blow open with a Sticky Bomb. Then escape the police. If you leave something behind, the operation comes back later, so it is not missable; you can return and finish the job. This is a good example of how the world trophies hide inside the illegal operations: the bowling itself is the cover for the robbery, and the trophy is about following through on the whole visit.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Method: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Reach maximum Strength with both Jason and Lucia together. This is a partnership trophy: it should pop when Jason and Lucia both reach maximum Strength, so buy a gym membership and train with your partner there, since the partner trains alongside you. The gym is the reliable way to build Strength, and training together means both characters progress at once instead of one at a time. There is no mission attached and nothing missable; gyms stay open after the story. The exact trigger is not yet fully confirmed in the game, so treat this as the community's best reading of the description: train together, max out Strength on both, and the trophy should follow.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Method: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make 500 choices that change your Criminal Profile. The counter tracks actions that change your profile, and robberies and fights feed it, so it fills up without a separate grind as long as you play the game the way the game wants you to: rob places, get into fights, make choices. Do not chase this trophy directly; it is designed to pop on its own somewhere in the middle of a normal playthrough, once the count reaches 500. If it has not popped by the time you finish the story, the fastest way to close the gap is a run of robberies and fights in free roam. There is nothing missable here, and the counter never resets.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 500) · Counter detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. The description is deliberately vague, and the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in the game, so this guide will not invent one. The honest reading is that the trophy rewards succeeding at something on a second attempt after failing it once, and the most likely candidates are the repeatable activities: a race, a challenge, a robbery or a stunt that you fail and then complete. If you fail something, do not reload an old save to erase the failure; retry it and see whether the trophy follows. This entry will be updated as the community pins the trigger down, and until then the advice is simply to keep retrying what you fail instead of avoiding it.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. The description is a shrug, and the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in the game, so this guide will not invent one. The honest reading is that the trophy is tied to one of the world's strange or unexplained moments, the kind of event you stumble across while exploring rather than something you can plan for. The practical advice is to explore the odd corners of Leonida, the remote spots, the late-night places and the things that look out of place, and to pay attention when something unusual happens instead of driving past it. As the community pins down the exact event, this entry will be updated; until then, keep exploring and keep your eyes open.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by. Get a melee weapon, get in a vehicle, and strike a pedestrian from the moving car, bowling them over as you pass. The name is a bowling joke, and the trophy is the drive-by version of the same idea: speed plus a melee swing, timed as you pass. Pick a quiet stretch of road with pedestrians, line up the pass, and swing as you go by. It is repeatable, so if the first attempt misses, circle around and try again. There is no mission attached and nothing missable; the only requirement is the melee weapon, the vehicle and the timing.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn 250,000 dollars laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from bank and payday loan jobs, and you launder them by selling them to your contacts. The total is cumulative, so every bill you launder adds to it, and the trophy pops at 250,000. The practical approach is to treat laundering as part of every robbery: take the marked bills from each job, sell them to your contacts as soon as you can, and let the counter climb alongside the vault and operation robberies. Do not hoard the bills; launder them regularly. Nothing here is missable, and the jobs that produce marked bills stay available after the story.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: $250,000) · Laundering detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend 100,000 dollars across all shops. The total is cumulative across every kind of shop, so everything you buy counts: weapons, clothes, food, car parts, whatever the shops sell. Most players will make good progress on this without trying, because a normal playthrough involves a lot of shopping, and the big purchases, the eight garages for Little Boxes cost about 160,000 dollars on their own, push the total a long way. The trophy pops at 100,000 spent. There is no need to waste money on things you do not want; just buy what you need as you play, and the counter will reach the target. Nothing is missable and the shops never close.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: $100,000) · Garage cost detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties. Buy the eight garages in the Vice City Real Estate app, which unlocks after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver. Together they cost about 160,000 dollars, so save up or sell what you do not need before you start buying. Garages the story gives you do not count, so only the purchased ones feed the counter. Each garage also gives you space to store vehicles, which matters for On the Spot, since every car you register needs a free garage space; buy the garages first, then register cheap cars. The trophy pops when the eighth garage is bought. Nothing is missable and the app stays open after the story.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade) · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 8) · App and cost detail: Output Lag trophy guide (outputlag.com) · Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The Chapter 2 mission Moses opens the app. Take a stolen car to Moses, choose Respray, then Register. From Chapter 3 you can also register cars with a standard tracker at Pay 'n' Spray. Each car needs a free garage space, so buy garages first, as Little Boxes asks, and register cheap cars rather than rare ones you want to keep. The counter climbs one car at a time, and the trophy pops at ten. There is nothing missable here, and the app stays open after the story, so this is a good cleanup trophy for the post-story phase, once the garages are bought and the map is open.
